title: LiuzLab/AI_MARRVEL pipeline parameters
description: AI-MARRVEL (AIM) is an AI system for rare genetic disease diagnosis.

input_phenopacket.description: Path to input phenopacket JSON file.

input_variant.description: Input variant in the format 'chrom-pos-ref-alt', e.g., '1-123456-A-T'.

input_ped.description: Path to the pedgree file for trio mode

storedir.description: Path to a shared directory for intermediate files. Reusing this directory across runs skips regenerating common files and cuts runtime.

ref_dir.description: Path to aim pipeline dependencies directory.

s3_bucket_data_name.description: [Not Implemented] S3 bucket name to aim pipeline dependencies directory.

bed_filter.description: Path to a BED file to perform an analysis only for regions of interest

exome_filter.description: Enable exonic filter. Addition will filter out variants outside of exonic region

impact_filter.description: Enable low impact. Addition will enable low impact transcripts.

vep_buffer_size.description: Largest VEP batch (--buffer_size); each task uses its variant count, at least 50 and at most this. Larger batches reload VEP's cache less often (on 17,533 variants with 2 forks, 1000 is 45% faster than 50) and use more memory, depending on how spread out a task's variants are (up to about 7 GB per task seen). Only VEP's HGNC_ID column, which AIM does not read, can depend on the size.

rust.description: Run PHRANK_SCORING, HPO_SIM, ANNOTATE_BY_MODULES, JOIN_PHRANK, ANNOTATE_TIER, MERGE_SCORES_BY_CHROMOSOME and PREDICTION with the Rust `aim` binary (see rust/README.md).

rust_vep.description: With --rust on hg38: run `aim vep` instead of VEP in ANNOTATE_BY_VEP (rows, consequences, HGVS, known variants and regulatory rows from the VEP cache; VEP's SIFT/PolyPhen/DOMAINS columns stay empty). Input it does not reproduce falls back to VEP.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.
